CRAS: cras_shm: split samples into separate shm Change the shm shared between client and server so that the samples area is mapped separately from the header. This will let us eventually transition to letting clients provide the shm to read samples from, if they so choose. The notable changes to the client/server protocol are: - change shm_max_size to samples_shm_size in stream_connected - append a header and a samples fd to stream_connected instead of the same header fd twice This commit maintains backwards compatibility, and does not change the rust cras_client. That change will be made in a separate commit. arc: networkd: Generalize ARC lifecycle notifications. This patch removes the signalling mechanism used to indicate when ARC++ starts and stops and replaces it with a simple text protocol over an abstract domain socket. This allows us to use the same upstart scripts without overlay for detecting both ARC++ and ARCVM. Recall this is intended to be temporary until the guests connect directly to the daemon. This change in turn requires message propagation to the child tasks (both adb proxy and ip helper) and the appropriate refactoring was done. The expansion of the protos is required anyway eventually to support notifications for multiple guests. Regenerate the mock owner public key and metric_{on,off} policies At some point, the acceptable format for the owner key changed, in terms of header sizes. This can be seen in commit d29ae33459d4 ("Updated policy_testserver to support verification key signatures"), in the chrome repo. Unfortunately, the code in this directory was not updated. As a result, if a user had logged into a test machine at any point before running platform_KernelErrorPaths (i.e. the machine has an owner), the test machine gets powerwashed and the test fails. The original code for generating the public key and the policy blobs is found attached to this document: https://sites.google.com/a/google.com/chromeos/archive/testing-tools-for-device-policies Along with it are the instructions to generate the keys. We follow these instructions and commit the updated code. TEST=platform_KernelErrorPaths.BUG passes after this. Tried running platform_KernelErrorPaths.ALL, but it has other issues. KernelErrorPaths: modify SysRQ-X test behaviour to match implementation Ever since the commit "CHROMIUM: sysrq: Stop trying to kill X server for 'X' key" sysrq-X can only be triggered twice in 20 seconds, before the machine reboots. Prior to that commit, sysrq-X would have to be triggered thrice, with the second instance killing the X server. The test continues to behave as if the old behaviour is in affect. This change modifies it to expect the new behaviour. BUG=chromium:966593 TEST=Ran platform_KernelErrorPaths.SYSRQ_X to make sure I didn't break anything else. But, I didn't reproduce this bug myself. Remove @allow_multiple_section_input decorator Certain RPC methods in FAFT were decorated with a custom property, @allow_multiple_section_input, which allowed multiple parameters to be bundled as a tuple. This change removes that custom solution. FAFT tests will now need to call the RPC multiple times in order to achieve the same effect. This change is particularly motivated by the upcoming protobuf, part of go/faft-grpc, which will define the parameters for all RPCs. It will be much clearer to read (section) than (section1, optional tuple_of_sections).
